baseline.why_this_is_a_cut_and_not_another_increm: The libgphoto2 pin is byte-identical to v105's -- 49b67fa44 -- so the camera stack a tester already has is unchanged and an upgrade over .105 is a straight overwrite. Every change in this cut is on the appliance side: the astro WebUI, the stage2 loader, the wifi station script, the release gate and the kit installer. Nothing here alters the solve path's inputs, the bundle layout or the catalogue.

purpose: Close the v105 field-test findings that are fixable in code we own, and stop the release process from shipping archives it never opened. Four defects reached main since .105: an empty Pentax choice list reported CAMERA_BUSY forever; polaris-apsta.sh down stopped nothing and left a dead resolver; the release gate verified a build directory instead of the archives a user actually receives; and a stale restart lock permanently blocked pgphoto restarts, quarantining a healthy K-3 III. Separately the astro WebUI's Apply-last button wrote a mount alignment from a solution the user could not see.

changes.summary: A permanently-empty choice list was reported to the app as CAMERA_BUSY. On the K-3 III exposurecompensation publishes no allowed-values list at all: the current value reads back but the list is empty, and the loader turned that into an infinite busy state rather than a terminal answer. It now returns the value with an empty list instead of retrying forever.

polaris-apsta.sh down stopped nothing and left a dead resolver behind. The stop path signalled the wrong process and never restored resolv.conf, so a station that was told to come down still appeared up to anything that asked.

The artifact gate now verifies the published archives rather than the build directory, and both producers invoke it. A verifier that reads a staging tree passes vacuously because out/ is gitignored; the gate now opens the zips a user receives. Wired into build-astro-candidate.sh and build-astro-bundle.sh so it runs on every build instead of being a check someone has to remember to call.
A stale restart lock permanently blocked pgphoto restarts, so a healthy K-3 III stayed quarantined until reboot. The lock is now reclaimed when its holder is gone.

Apply-last states what it is about to write and never reports an unconfirmed write as success. #solve-apply posted an empty body, showed nothing on success and only a bare error string on failure, so the user wrote a mount alignment from a solution whose RA/Dec, roll and pixel scale were never displayed -- although /api/state already returns the whole solver JSON and /api/apply already reports age_sec. The decision table moved to container/astro/webui/solve-apply.js, DOM-free like shutter.js, asserted under node.

The kit install is scripted and every release entrypoint is indexed. install-astro-kit.sh stages a candidate over tar+ssh, verifies every byte against ASTRO-MANIFEST.sha256, runs install_astro.sh, reboots for the boot hook and fails closed unless :8090 is serving. docs/RELEASE-ENTRYPOINTS.md indexes operation to command, with a test asserting no scripts/release/ script goes unindexed.

known_limits: The libgphoto2 pin is unchanged from v105 (49b67fa44). No driver change is included, because the six pgphoto issues filed against v105 (#323-#328) do not reproduce at the library boundary and libgphoto2's own AGENTS.md forbids a driver change for a consumer-discovered failure without a repo-local reproducer.

The #323-#328 claims were checked against the shipped binaries and found unimplementable as specified: the cited helpers are static and not exported from ptp2.so, params->pentax.vendor_mode_enabled is internal to the camlib and unreachable from pgphoto's public API, and both public config entry points already funnel into the guarded _put_ handlers. Corrections are pending on those issues.

The #329 fix is verified by execution under node (17 assertion groups, mutation-checked) but not on hardware: no mount was reachable during development, so 'alignment written' reflects what /api/apply reported rather than independently confirmed mount state.
Issue #251 remains release-blocking for the standard camera owner.
The K-3 III recognition fault (#297) is diagnosed to layer 3 and not yet fixed; this cut carries the read-only diagnostics only.
validation_focus: K-3 III exposurecompensation: the control must answer rather than reporting busy forever.
polaris-apsta.sh down: the station must actually come down and resolv.conf must be restored.
Release archives: open polaris-astro.zip and polaris-wifi.zip from the finished candidate and confirm the exec bits and wifi licence files are present in the archive, not just on disk.
pgphoto restart: clear a stale restart lock and confirm pgphoto comes back without a reboot.
Astro WebUI Apply-last: it must name the solution before writing and report the frame age afterwards; with no solve performed it must refuse and say why.
